I traced all 9 tests through the new code and they pass, with no test-specific logic. Rule 1 (keep mixed-case words like "iPhone" and "NASA" as written) now runs first, which also fixes a leading "iPhone" (the old code turned it into "Iphone"). The `index < last_index` check adds the last-word exception the docstring already required. Trailing-punctuation matching ("in,") still works. The `capitalize()` call is safe because any word with an uppercase letter after its first character has already been handled by Rule 1.

The original docstring clashed with `test_subtitle_after_colon`: under its rules, "a" after "Field:" should stay lowercase, but the test expects "A". Because the tests are the agreed spec, the agent added a general subtitle-after-colon rule (standard Chicago style) and documented it in both the docstring and the PR description. That's the right fix, not a special case for one test. Since it changes the spec, a quick confirmation from the editorial team would be good.

Minor follow-ups (not blocking): the colon check only looks at the character at the very end of a word, so it misses cases like "field:)". It also doesn't handle other subtitle separators such as em dashes.
